Old units of length, small to big.Barleycorn: Medieval English law treated three of these grains, dry and round, laid end to end as one inch, a rule dating back to the 1300s.
Old units of length, small to big.Inch: The word comes from the Latin for twelfth, as a foot was once divided into twelve. It was also once the width of a thumb.
Old units of length, small to big.Palm: Roughly the width of an open hand, it survives today in the 'palm' of a hand and in an old measure used in craftsmen's trade.
Old units of length, small to big.Hand: Still used today to measure horses' height at the withers, so a fifteen-hand horse stands exactly sixty inches tall.
Old units of length, small to big.Span: Measured from thumb tip to little finger tip with the hand stretched wide, it was a handy body-based measure before rulers were common.
Old units of length, small to big.Foot: Based on the length of a human foot, this unit differed from town to town for centuries until national standards finally fixed it.
Old units of length, small to big.Cubit: From the Latin for elbow, this ancient measure runs from the elbow to the fingertip and was used from Egypt to Mesopotamia.
Old units of length, small to big.Yard: Legend says it came from the distance between King Henry I's nose and his outstretched thumb, though its true origin is murkier.
Old units of length, small to big.English ell: Used by English cloth merchants to measure fabric, it was based on the length of an arm and is why textile units sound so unusual today.
Old units of length, small to big.Fathom: Sailors still use this unit to measure water depth, and it is based on the span of a man's outstretched arms.

When these US presidents first took offi.George Washington: The only president elected unanimously by the Electoral College, and he did it twice. He stepped down after two terms.
When these US presidents first took offi.Thomas Jefferson: He won after a tied electoral vote with Aaron Burr, which the House of Representatives had to resolve.
When these US presidents first took offi.Andrew Jackson: The first president from outside Virginia or Massachusetts, he came from Tennessee and campaigned as a man of the people.
When these US presidents first took offi.Abraham Lincoln: He took office with seven states already seceded, and the Civil War began just weeks later at Fort Sumter.
When these US presidents first took offi.Theodore Roosevelt: He became president at 42 after McKinley's assassination, the youngest in US history. 'Teddy bear' is named after him.
When these US presidents first took offi.Franklin D. Roosevelt: The only president elected four times. The 22nd Amendment later limited presidents to two terms.
When these US presidents first took offi.Dwight D. Eisenhower: A five-star general who helped plan D-Day, he warned of the 'military-industrial complex' in his farewell address.
When these US presidents first took offi.John F. Kennedy: The youngest elected president at 43 and the first Catholic, he was assassinated in Dallas in 1963.
When these US presidents first took offi.Richard Nixon: The only president to resign, in 1974, rather than face impeachment over the Watergate scandal.
When these US presidents first took offi.Ronald Reagan: A former Hollywood actor and California governor, he was shot 69 days into his first term and recovered.

North American animals by weight.Eastern chipmunk: Its cheek pouches can swell to several times the size of its head, which helps it haul food to its burrow.
North American animals by weight.Black-tailed prairie dog: Their alarm calls are complex enough that researchers believe they can describe a predator's size and even shape.
North American animals by weight.Striped skunk: The spray can reach about 3 m, and its sulphur compounds are so potent that the smell lingers for days.
North American animals by weight.Raccoon: Its sensitive front paws have a huge number of nerve endings, and it seems to 'wash' food as it feels it.
North American animals by weight.Coyote: It spread across the continent as wolves disappeared, and now lives in big cities like Chicago and New York.
North American animals by weight.Cougar: It has the largest range of any wild land mammal in the Americas, from the Yukon to the southern Andes.
North American animals by weight.American black bear: Not always black: colours range to cinnamon, and the white 'spirit bear' of British Columbia is a black bear subspecies.
North American animals by weight.Grizzly bear: Its name comes from 'grizzled', for the silver-tipped fur, and it spends winter in a den.
North American animals by weight.Moose: The largest deer, a bull's antlers can span up to about 1.8 m and are regrown every year.
North American animals by weight.American bison: The largest land mammal in North America. It once numbered tens of millions before hunting nearly wiped it out in the 1800s.

When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Espresso machine patent: Angelo Moriondo of Turin patented the machine, and it was later improved by Bezzera and Pavoni.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Decaffeination process: Ludwig Roselius developed it after his father died, thinking caffeine was to blame, and it was sold as Sanka.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Tea bag: The story goes that New York merchant Thomas Sullivan sent samples in silk pouches, and customers brewed them whole.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Nescafé instant coffee: Nestlé developed it after Brazil sought help with its surplus of coffee, and soldiers in WWII spread it.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Irish coffee: Joe Sheridan made it for cold passengers at Foynes airport, from coffee, whiskey, sugar and cream.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Mr. Coffee drip machine: Vincent Marotta launched the machine and hired baseball star Joe DiMaggio as the pitchman.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Starbucks Frappuccino: It came from Boston's Coffee Connection, bought by Starbucks, which then launched the drink.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Keurig K-Cup: Its inventor John Sylvan later said he regretted the waste from the single-use pods.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Pumpkin Spice Latte: The seasonal latte was developed by a Starbucks team and tested in Vancouver and Washington before launch.
When these coffee and tea innovations ar.Dalgona coffee craze: Named for a Korean honeycomb toffee, it went viral in lockdown as a whipped-coffee trend.

Firsts for women in science.Caroline Herschel's comet: She found eight comets, and was the first woman to discover one, with her brother William's telescope.
Firsts for women in science.Mary Anning's ichthyosaur: As a child, the Lyme Regis fossil hunter found a skeleton of a sea reptile, though the Geological Society barred her.
Firsts for women in science.Elizabeth Blackwell's MD: Geneva Medical College students reportedly voted to admit her, thinking it was a joke.
Firsts for women in science.Marie Curie's first Nobel: The 1903 Physics prize she shared with her husband Pierre and Becquerel was the first of her two Nobels.
Firsts for women in science.Meitner explains fission: She worked out how the atom splits with her nephew Otto Frisch, but only Otto Hahn won the Nobel; element 109 bears her name.
Firsts for women in science.First women Royal Society FRS: The Royal Society chose Kathleen Lonsdale and Marjory Stephenson after nearly three centuries of only men.
Firsts for women in science.Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51: Her X-ray image of DNA gave Watson and Crick a vital clue, and she died in 1958 aged just 37.
Firsts for women in science.Mirzakhani wins Fields Medal: The Iranian mathematician was the first woman to win the Fields Medal, and she died young in 2017.
Firsts for women in science.Tu Youyou wins Nobel: She found artemisinin, a malaria drug, in an ancient Chinese herbal text and has no doctorate.
Firsts for women in science.Doudna and Charpentier Nobel: They developed CRISPR gene editing, and were the first all-female team to win a science Nobel.

Native speakers of these languages (appr.Icelandic: Icelandic speakers can read medieval sagas almost directly, and they coin new words from native roots rather than borrowing.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Latvian: This Baltic language is among the most conservative of Europe's Indo-European languages.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Danish: Fifty is halvtreds, short for a phrase meaning half-third-times-twenty, as Danes count in twenties.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Greek: Its written record spans about 3,400 years, from Linear B tablets to today.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Dutch: English got words like cookie, yacht and boss from Dutch.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Italian: Dante's Tuscan dialect became the base of standard Italian, in a country that had no single language for centuries.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Japanese: It mixes three scripts at once: kanji, hiragana and katakana.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Hindi: Spoken Hindi is almost the same as Urdu, with different scripts and vocabulary.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Spanish: After Mandarin it is the world's second most spoken native language, ahead of English.
Native speakers of these languages (appr.Mandarin: Based on the Beijing dialect, it has four tones, and a syllable like ma can mean four different things.

Units of distance.Metre: It was first defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from pole to equator, and now by the speed of light.
Units of distance.Rod: Also called a pole or perch, it measured 16.5 feet and was used by surveyors.
Units of distance.Chain: A cricket pitch is exactly one of them, 22 yards, and the unit survives in railway distances.
Units of distance.Furlong: Its name means furrow long, the distance an ox team could plow before resting, and horse racing still uses it.
Units of distance.Kilometre: Born in the French Revolution's metric system, it is a thousand meters.
Units of distance.Mile: It comes from Latin mille passus, a thousand paces, as measured by Roman soldiers.
Units of distance.Nautical mile: It equals one minute of latitude, and a knot is one of them per hour.
Units of distance.League: In Jules Verne's novel, 20,000 of them is the distance traveled under the sea, not the depth.
Units of distance.Scandinavian mile: Swedes and Norwegians still use mil in everyday speech for ten kilometers.
Units of distance.Marathon: The distance was fixed after the 1908 London Olympics, when the course was stretched so it finished before the royal box.

When these famous duels were fought.Button Gwinnett vs. McIntosh: A signer of the Declaration of Independence, he died days after being shot; his autograph is among the rarest and priciest in America.
When these famous duels were fought.Hamilton vs. Burr: Hamilton, a former Treasury secretary, died the next day; Burr was the sitting vice president.
When these famous duels were fought.Andrew Jackson vs. Dickinson: Jackson took a bullet near the heart and carried it for life, but he killed Dickinson.
When these famous duels were fought.Stephen Decatur vs. Barron: The naval hero was killed at Bladensburg, Maryland, a famous dueling ground outside Washington.
When these famous duels were fought.Wellington vs. Winchilsea: Wellington was prime minister when he fought it, over insults about Catholic emancipation; neither man was hurt.
When these famous duels were fought.Évariste Galois's fatal duel: The mathematical prodigy died at 20; he reportedly scribbled down his ideas on group theory the night before.
When these famous duels were fought.Pushkin's fatal duel: Russia's national poet died at 37 after defending his wife's honour against a French officer.
When these famous duels were fought.Lermontov's fatal duel: The author of A Hero of Our Time died at 26, four years after Pushkin, in a similar quarrel.
When these famous duels were fought.Lincoln vs. Shields (aborted): As the challenged party, Lincoln chose cavalry broadswords, and friends intervened before blood was drawn.
When these famous duels were fought.Gaston Defferre vs. Ribière: The Marseille mayor fought a deputy with swords; Ribiere was wounded, in one of France's last such duels.

How deep can they dive?.Great cormorant: Its feathers soak up water, which helps it dive; afterward it spreads its wings to dry.
How deep can they dive?.Atlantic puffin: It uses its wings to 'fly' underwater, and can carry many fish crosswise in its beak.
How deep can they dive?.Sea otter: It has the densest fur of any animal, up to about a million hairs per square inch.
How deep can they dive?.Human freediver (record): Herbert Nitsch's no-limits dive in 2012 set this record, which took him deep with a weighted sled.
How deep can they dive?.Bottlenose dolphin: Its lungs can collapse at depth, moving air into rigid airways, which helps avoid decompression problems.
How deep can they dive?.Emperor penguin: It is the deepest-diving bird, staying under for over 20 minutes.
How deep can they dive?.Leatherback turtle: The deepest-diving turtle has no hard shell, only leathery skin over flexible bone.
How deep can they dive?.Narwhal: The male's tusk is a spiralled tooth up to 3 metres long, packed with sensory nerves.
How deep can they dive?.Cuvier's beaked whale: It holds the record for the deepest, longest mammal dive, staying down over three hours.
How deep can they dive?.Snailfish (deepest fish seen): This tiny, gelatinous fish was filmed in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench in 2022, near the limit scientists think fish can survive.

When these railway bridges opened.Britannia Bridge, Wales: Robert Stephenson's tubular iron bridge over the Menai Strait was rebuilt after a 1970 fire.
When these railway bridges opened.Royal Albert Bridge: Brunel's bridge over the Tamar at Saltash; he was too ill to attend the opening and died months later.
When these railway bridges opened.Ribblehead Viaduct: This 24-arch Yorkshire Dales viaduct was threatened with closure in the 1980s but was saved.
When these railway bridges opened.Garabit Viaduct, France: Designed by Gustave Eiffel before his famous tower, this arch viaduct crosses the Truyere river.
When these railway bridges opened.Forth Bridge: This red cantilever bridge gave us the idiom for a never-ending task: 'painting the Forth Bridge'.
When these railway bridges opened.Glenfinnan Viaduct: It appears in the Harry Potter films as the Hogwarts Express route.
When these railway bridges opened.Landwasser Viaduct: A curved limestone viaduct in the Swiss Alps emerging straight from a tunnel, it is a UNESCO site.
When these railway bridges opened.Victoria Falls Bridge: Part of Cecil Rhodes's dream of a Cape to Cairo railway, it spans the Zambezi gorge between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
When these railway bridges opened.Pamban Bridge, India: It joins Rameswaram island to the mainland, and a central section lifted for ships.
When these railway bridges opened.Quebec Bridge: It collapsed twice during construction, in 1907 and 1916, killing 88 workers, before finally opening.

Battery sizes by diameter.AAAA: Used in stylus pens and small flashlights, it is a tiny cylinder, a bit thinner than an AAA.
Battery sizes by diameter.AAA: Found in remote controls and many small gadgets, it is a size that took off with portable devices in the 1960s.
Battery sizes by diameter.LR44 button cell: A button cell used in calculators, toys and laser pointers, and swallowed ones are a serious danger to small children.
Battery sizes by diameter.AA: The world's most common household battery, it is a 1.5 volt alkaline size used in everything from clocks to controllers.
Battery sizes by diameter.CR123A camera battery: This lithium cell is used in flashlights and cameras, and has a shelf life of about ten years.
Battery sizes by diameter.CR2032 coin cell: Its code shows a 20 mm diameter and 3.2 mm thickness, and it is found in key fobs, watches and motherboards.
Battery sizes by diameter.Sub-C power-tool cell: Used in cordless drills, usually as NiCd cells, they gave power tools their first long run time.
Battery sizes by diameter.C: Once common in big flashlights and boomboxes, it sits between AA and D in size.
Battery sizes by diameter.D: The D cell dates from 1898, when Eveready introduced it for flashlights, and it is still used in big torches and radios.
Battery sizes by diameter.6-volt lantern battery: It has spring terminals and was once used in camp lanterns, and it is much bigger than other cells, about the size of a brick.

Television technology milestones.Baird's mechanical TV demo: John Logie Baird's mechanical television used a spinning disc, and his 1926 demonstration in London showed moving images to scientists.
Television technology milestones.US color TV broadcasts: Color broadcasts began in the US in 1954, though few families could afford sets, and color only became standard in the 1960s.
Television technology milestones.First wireless TV remote: The first wireless remote, called the Flash-Matic, used a beam of light, but sunlight confused it and caused random channel changes.
Television technology milestones.Ceefax teletext: Ceefax was the BBC's teletext service, delivering news, sport and weather as blocky text pages, and many viewers loved it.
Television technology milestones.Consumer plasma TV: Plasma TVs lit up tiny cells of gas, and they were thin enough to hang on a wall, though they were heavy and power-hungry.
Television technology milestones.US HDTV broadcasts: High-definition broadcasts in the US began in 1998, but it took years before most households owned a set that could show it.
Television technology milestones.First OLED TV: OLED TVs have pixels that make their own light, so blacks can be perfectly dark, and Sony's first one was only 11 inches wide.
Television technology milestones.Consumer 3D TVs: Consumer 3D TVs arrived with the hit film Avatar, but they faded within a few years as viewers disliked wearing glasses.
Television technology milestones.Consumer 4K TVs: 4K sets have four times the pixels of Full HD, and prices fell fast, so 4K became the normal choice within about a decade.
Television technology milestones.Consumer 8K TVs: 8K TVs have around 33 million pixels, more than the human eye can distinguish from typical viewing distances.

Fictional house numbers.The Addams Family: In the 1960s sitcom, the address was a joke on the family's spooky tastes and fits their cemetery-side home.
Fictional house numbers.The Dursleys: Harry spent years sleeping in the cupboard under its stairs, until letters from Hogwarts arrived.
Fictional house numbers.Sirius Black's house: The Order of the Phoenix's headquarters is hidden by magic between the number 11 and 13 muggle houses.
Fictional house numbers.Paddington's Browns: Paddington, the Peruvian bear, was found at the railway station, and now lives here with the Brown family.
Fictional house numbers.SpongeBob: It's a pineapple under the sea in the underwater city of Bikini Bottom.
Fictional house numbers.Sherlock Holmes: When the stories were written no such address existed, and later a bank employed a secretary to answer letters to Holmes.
Fictional house numbers.The Simpsons: Springfield's state is never confirmed, a long-running running gag, so their address leaves out a zip.
Fictional house numbers.The Munsters: The 1960s sitcom's gothic house hosted a family of friendly monsters, and the show ran in black and white.
Fictional house numbers.Sheldon and Leonard: Its exterior was a real ordinary house in Studio City, California, which HGTV bought and renovated in 2018.
Fictional house numbers.The Brady Bunch: Apartment 4A is in Pasadena, California, a real city that is home to Caltech, the real-life science institute.

Milestones in treating the mind.Mesmer's animal magnetism: Franz Mesmer's cures by magnetic fluid were debunked by a royal commission including Benjamin Franklin, yet gave us the word mesmerise.
Milestones in treating the mind.Pinel unchains asylum patients: Philippe Pinel's reforms at Paris hospitals are a landmark in humane care, though historians debate how much he personally unchained.
Milestones in treating the mind.Dorothea Dix's asylum appeal: After seeing mentally ill people jailed, Dix lobbied state after state for humane hospitals, starting with her Massachusetts appeal.
Milestones in treating the mind.Studies on Hysteria: Josef Breuer and Sigmund Freud's book introduced the talking cure, a founding step of psychoanalysis, based on the patient Anna O.
Milestones in treating the mind.First lobotomy: Portuguese neurologist Egas Moniz shared the 1949 Nobel Prize for developing it, an award later widely criticised.
Milestones in treating the mind.First electroshock therapy: Italian doctors Cerletti and Bini first used it, and modern ECT, given under anaesthesia, remains effective for severe depression.
Milestones in treating the mind.Lithium for mania: Australian psychiatrist John Cade found that this simple salt calmed mania, and lithium remains a mainstay for bipolar disorder.
Milestones in treating the mind.Chlorpromazine: Originally studied as a surgical aid in France, it became the first widely used antipsychotic and helped empty the old asylums.
Milestones in treating the mind.Beck Depression Inventory: Psychiatrist Aaron Beck's 21-question questionnaire became one of the most widely used tools for gauging depression severity.
Milestones in treating the mind.Esketamine nasal spray: Sold as Spravato and derived from the anaesthetic ketamine, it offers rapid relief for hard-to-treat depression under clinic supervision.

TV drama premieres.Dallas: Texas-set Dallas made 'Who shot J.R.?' the biggest question of 1980, and the answer episode drew about 80 million American viewers.
TV drama premieres.Miami Vice: This crime drama's style popularized pastel suits and a synth score, and produced Don Johnson's stubble look in the mid-1980s.
TV drama premieres.Twin Peaks: David Lynch and Mark Frost's mystery began with the question 'Who killed Laura Palmer?', and the series is known for its dancing dwarf and its damn fine coffee.
TV drama premieres.ER: Set in a Chicago hospital, it was created by novelist Michael Crichton, and it made a star out of George Clooney.
TV drama premieres.The West Wing: Aaron Sorkin's White House drama won a record nine Emmys in its first season, and its fast-talking 'walk and talk' scenes became a TV trademark.
TV drama premieres.Lost: The pilot, with its plane crash, was one of the most expensive ever, and the show's 'numbers' and polar bear mysteries drove many a fan theory.
TV drama premieres.Mad Men: Matthew Weiner's ad-agency drama was the first basic-cable show to win the Emmy for outstanding drama series, and it was set in the 1960s.
TV drama premieres.Breaking Bad: Walter White, a chemistry teacher turned drug maker, grew from a mild teacher into a kingpin, and the show's finale in 2013 was widely praised.
TV drama premieres.Downton Abbey: This costume drama about the Crawley family and their servants was shown in over 200 territories, and it became one of the most watched British exports.
TV drama premieres.Stranger Things: The Duffer brothers' Netflix show, set in 1980s Indiana, paid tribute to Spielberg and Stephen King, and revived Kate Bush's 'Running Up That Hill' in 2022.

When these coffee brands were founded.Folgers: Folgers was founded by William Folger in San Francisco, and its ads about 'the best part of waking up' are famous.
When these coffee brands were founded.Maxwell House: Maxwell House was named after a Nashville hotel, and Theodore Roosevelt reportedly said it was 'good to the last drop'.
When these coffee brands were founded.Lavazza: Lavazza, from Turin, was started as a grocery shop, and pioneered the idea of blending coffees from different origins.
When these coffee brands were founded.illy: illy created a single blend and the first pressurized coffee tin, and its logo was drawn by artist James Rosenquist.
When these coffee brands were founded.Nescafé: Nescafé, created by Nestlé after Brazil asked for help with its coffee surplus, was an early instant coffee.
When these coffee brands were founded.Tim Hortons: Tim Hortons, founded by a hockey player, became a Canadian symbol, and Timbits are its donut holes.
When these coffee brands were founded.Peet's Coffee: Peet's Coffee in Berkeley was founded by Alfred Peet, who taught the founders of Starbucks about dark roast.
When these coffee brands were founded.Costa Coffee: Costa Coffee was started by two Italian brothers in London, and now has thousands of shops.
When these coffee brands were founded.Nespresso: Nespresso brought capsule coffee to homes, and its machines were developed by Nestlé.
When these coffee brands were founded.Blue Bottle Coffee: Blue Bottle, founded by a clarinetist, was named after Europe's first coffee house, and was bought by Nestlé in 2017.

Medical devices, by when they were intro.Eyeglasses: Spectacles appeared in northern Italy around 1286, and no one knows who invented them.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.Stethoscope: René Laennec invented it in Paris because he felt it improper to press his ear to a woman's chest, so he rolled paper into a tube.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.Hypodermic syringe: Alexander Wood in Edinburgh and Charles Pravaz in France developed it around the same time, independently.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.X-ray imaging: Wilhelm Röntgen X-rayed his wife's hand, ring visible, and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.Electrocardiogram (ECG): Willem Einthoven built the string galvanometer that recorded the heart's electricity, earning a Nobel Prize in 1924.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.Iron lung: It helped polio patients whose chest muscles were paralyzed to breathe, by changing air pressure around the body.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.Defibrillator (first human): Claude Beck in Cleveland first used it on a 14-year-old boy during surgery in 1947, and the boy survived.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.Implanted pacemaker: Swedish patient Arne Larsson was first to receive one and went on to get 26 over his life, outliving its inventor.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.CT scanner (first patient): Godfrey Hounsfield developed it at EMI, the same record company that sold the Beatles' records.
Medical devices, by when they were intro.MRI (first human scan): The first human scan, by Raymond Damadian's team, took almost five hours to produce a single image.

Capital cities by elevation.Baku: The Caspian Sea, on which it sits, itself lies below ocean level. Baku is also a long-time oil-boom city.
Capital cities by elevation.London: The tidal Thames runs up past the city to Teddington, and the Thames Barrier protects London from storm surges.
Capital cities by elevation.Moscow: Moscow lies on a low plain along the Moscow River, yet Russians claim it too is built on seven hills, like Rome.
Capital cities by elevation.Bern: Its old town sits in a tight loop of the Aare river and is a UNESCO site. Einstein worked in a patent office here.
Capital cities by elevation.Madrid: The highest capital in the European Union, perched on a plateau in central Spain.
Capital cities by elevation.Yerevan: The Pink City is built of volcanic tuff, and is among the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, founded in 782 BC.
Capital cities by elevation.Harare: Called Salisbury until 1982, it is known as the Sunshine City for its mild highland climate and jacaranda-lined streets.
Capital cities by elevation.Nairobi: The name comes from a Maasai phrase for cool water. It is the only capital with a national park inside its borders.
Capital cities by elevation.Addis Ababa: The name means "new flower". It is the seat of the African Union and one of the highest capitals in the world.
Capital cities by elevation.La Paz: The highest seat of government in the world; the airport sits even higher, at over 4,000 meters. Sucre is Bolivia's official capital.

Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Б (be): Б was invented for the b sound, while the Greek-derived В took over the v sound, which is why Russian reads "Bob" and "Vova" differently.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Г (ge): It descends from the Greek gamma, but in Russian it sounds like a hard g, and in the endings of surnames like Tolstogo it is read as v.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Ж (zhe): This letter was invented for the Slavic zh sound, like the s in "measure", which Greek had no letter for.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.И (i): It looks like a backward N to English eyes, and it makes an ee sound; adding a small curve on top gives Й, the short i.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Л (el): It resembles the Greek lambda, its ancestor, and the letter is the l in the Russian name for Lenin, Ленин.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.П (pe): Its shape is the Greek pi, and it makes the same p sound, so Russian Пушкин, the poet Pushkin, begins with a gateway.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Ф (ef): Descended from the Greek phi, it is rare in native Slavic words and mostly appears in borrowings such as фильм, film.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Ц (tse): It begins the word for tsar, spelled царь, and it makes a ts sound that Russian speakers can start words with easily.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Ш (sha): Its shape may have come from the Hebrew letter shin, which makes the same sh sound, via the older Glagolitic alphabet.
Russian Cyrillic letters, in alphabet or.Я (ya): It is both the last letter of the alphabet and the Russian word for I, so the last letter literally means me.

Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Gold: Rare enough that all the gold ever mined would fill only a few Olympic swimming pools.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Silver: It carries electricity and heat better than any other metal, which is why it appears in fine electronics and solar panels.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Copper: The Statue of Liberty's green skin is copper that has weathered over the decades into a protective patina.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Carbon: Though only about 0.02 percent of the crust, it is the backbone of all known life.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Titanium: Strong, light and corrosion-resistant, it is among the ten most common elements in the crust, but is hard to extract.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Calcium: The main component of limestone and chalk, and the mineral that hardens your bones and teeth.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Iron: Most of Earth's iron sits in its core, so the crust holds only a minor share of the planet's iron.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Aluminium: The most abundant metal in the crust, yet once costlier than gold because it was so hard to extract from its ore.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Silicon: It is the main component of sand and most rocks, locked into silicate minerals, and also the base of microchips.
Elements in Earth's crust by abundance.Oxygen: Nearly half the crust by weight is oxygen, mostly locked inside minerals rather than floating free as the gas we breathe.

Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.Q: Q is among the rarest letters in English, and it is almost always followed by u.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.W: Its English name, 'double u', recalls how it was written as two Vs joined together, as French 'double vé' still says.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.E: The most common letter in English, yet Georges Perec wrote a whole 1969 novel, La Disparition, without it.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.R: The layout's odd arrangement dates from 1870s typewriters, where it kept frequently paired typebars from jamming.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.T: All the letters of the word TYPEWRITER sit on this single row, a famous quirk of the layout.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.Y: On German QWERTZ keyboards, Y and Z swap places, since Z is far more common than Y in German.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.U: Four of the five vowels live on this row, E, U, I and O, with only A down on the home row.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.I: The dot above a lowercase i has its own name: the tittle.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.O: It began as a Phoenician letter that meant 'eye', and its round shape has barely changed since.
Letters on a QWERTY keyboard's top row.P: It's typed with the pinky, the weakest finger, a burden the alternative Dvorak layout tried to spread more evenly.

Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Apophis skims past Earth: The asteroid Apophis will pass about 32,000 km from Earth on a Friday the 13th in April, closer than many satellites, visible to the naked eye.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Coast-to-coast US eclipse: On August 12, the Moon's shadow will sweep from California to Florida, the first US coast-to-coast total eclipse since 1918.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Halley's Comet returns: Halley's Comet comes by about every 76 years. It was last seen in 1986 and was the first comet shown to return, as Edmond Halley predicted.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Next transit of Venus: Transits of Venus come in pairs eight years apart, with over a century between pairs. Captain Cook sailed to Tahiti to watch the 1769 one.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Pluto finishes 1st orbit seen: Pluto takes about 248 Earth years to circle the Sun. Discovered in 1930, it completes its first full orbit since discovery in 2178.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Vega becomes the pole star: Earth's axis wobbles over about 26,000 years, so the north star changes. Today it's Polaris, but the bright blue-white star Vega will take over.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Voyager 1 nears Gliese 445: Launched in 1977, the probe is the most distant human-made object. In roughly 40,000 years it will pass within about 1.6 light-years of this red dwarf.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.Earth's oceans boil away: As the Sun slowly brightens, it will eventually evaporate the seas. Earth's surface will become far too hot for liquid water in about a billion years.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.The Sun becomes a red giant: Its core will run out of hydrogen, and the Sun will swell to many times its size, probably swallowing Mercury and Venus and scorching the Earth.
Predicted sky events and cosmic futures.The last stars burn out: The smallest red dwarf stars burn so slowly that they can shine for trillions of years, so the final glow is a vastly distant future.

Microsoft products by debut.MS-DOS: Microsoft bought the system from Seattle Computer Products and licensed it to IBM for its first PC.
Microsoft products by debut.Microsoft Word: Its first version ran on DOS, and the Windows version in 1989 helped it take over.
Microsoft products by debut.Excel: It first appeared for the Macintosh in 1985, not for Windows.
Microsoft products by debut.PowerPoint: A startup called Forethought made it, and Microsoft bought the company in 1987 for about $14 million.
Microsoft products by debut.Encarta: This encyclopedia on CD-ROM was shut down in 2009, outcompeted by Wikipedia.
Microsoft products by debut.Internet Explorer: It debuted in the Microsoft Plus pack for Windows 95, and at its peak it was used by over 90% of web users.
Microsoft products by debut.Xbox: Halo: Combat Evolved launched with it and helped it become a flagship console.
Microsoft products by debut.Bing: Microsoft's search engine replaced Live Search in 2009, its answer to Google.
Microsoft products by debut.Surface: Microsoft's first own-brand computer, it began with the Surface RT tablet.
Microsoft products by debut.Microsoft Copilot: It is an AI assistant built on OpenAI's models, put into Windows and Office.

What's dissolved in seawater?.Fluoride: The same element sits in toothpaste, and it occurs in seawater at only a few parts per million.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Boron: Desalination plants must remove it, since even small amounts harm boron-sensitive crops irrigated with the water.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Strontium: Some tiny plankton called acantharians build their skeletons from strontium sulfate, which is unusual among living things.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Bromide: Antoine Balard found bromine in 1826 while studying salt-marsh brines from the Mediterranean coast of France.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Bicarbonate: It acts as a buffer that helps keep the ocean's acidity steady as it absorbs carbon dioxide from the air.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Calcium: Corals, clams and plankton pull it out of the water to build skeletons and shells.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Magnesium: Seawater is an important source of magnesium metal, which is extracted commercially from the ocean.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Sulfate: Bacteria in seafloor mud use it to breathe, producing the rotten egg smell of sulfide.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Sodium: It makes up roughly 30 percent of the dissolved salts, and it is the cation in table salt.
What's dissolved in seawater?.Chloride: It is the most abundant dissolved ion, making up over half of the salts that give the sea its taste.

When these skyscrapers were completed.Home Insurance Bldg, Chicago: Often called the first skyscraper, it used a metal frame to carry the weight, rising ten storeys at first.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Flatiron Building: Its triangular shape is said to have caused wind gusts that blew up ladies' skirts, giving rise to the phrase '23 skidoo'.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Woolworth Building: Nicknamed the Cathedral of Commerce, it was the world's tallest building until 1930. Its owner paid for it in cash.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Chrysler Building: It held the title of tallest building for only months before the Empire State Building. Its steel spire was secretly raised through the roof.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Empire State Building: Built in about 13 months, it kept the title of world's tallest for nearly 40 years.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Seagram Building: Mies van der Rohe's bronze-and-glass tower became the model of sleek International Style office buildings.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Sears (Willis) Tower: The tallest building in the world for about 25 years. It was renamed Willis Tower in 2009.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Petronas Towers: These twin towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004, linked by a sky bridge.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Taipei 101: A giant golden steel ball hung inside acts as a tuned mass damper to calm swaying in typhoons and earthquakes.
When these skyscrapers were completed.Burj Khalifa: At around 828 metres, it is the tallest building in the world, with the top visible from many kilometres away.

Turning points in southern African histo.Dutch found Cape Town: Jan van Riebeeck set up a supply station for Dutch East India Company ships, planting the seed of European colonization.
Turning points in southern African histo.Shaka becomes Zulu king: He remade the Zulu army with short stabbing spears and tight formations, turning a small clan into a powerful kingdom.
Turning points in southern African histo.Great Trek begins: Thousands of Boer settlers left the British-ruled Cape and moved inland, founding republics like the Transvaal.
Turning points in southern African histo.Berlin Conference: European powers set rules for carving up Africa at a conference with no African delegates, driving the 'Scramble for Africa'.
Turning points in southern African histo.Battle of Adwa: Ethiopian forces defeated invading Italians, preserving independence and making Ethiopia a symbol of resistance to colonialism.
Turning points in southern African histo.Second Boer War begins: Britain fought the Boer republics and used camps where tens of thousands of civilians died, mostly from disease.
Turning points in southern African histo.ANC founded: Founded in Bloemfontein, it later led the struggle against apartheid, and Nelson Mandela became its best-known leader.
Turning points in southern African histo.Apartheid begins: The National Party won the election and began writing racial segregation into law, which lasted until the early 1990s.
Turning points in southern African histo.Mandela sentenced to life: At his trial he said he was prepared to die for his ideals; he spent 27 years in prison, much of it on Robben Island.
Turning points in southern African histo.Rwandan genocide: In about 100 days in 1994, hundreds of thousands, mostly Tutsi, were killed; it ended when the RPF took Kigali.

Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Marlee Matlin: She won for Children of a Lesser God (1986), her film debut, and remains the youngest Best Actress winner; she is deaf, like her character.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Jennifer Lawrence: She won for Silver Linings Playbook, and tripped on the steps while walking up to accept, then joked about it on stage.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Adrien Brody: His win for The Pianist made him the youngest Best Actor winner ever, and in 2025 he won again for The Brutalist.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Eddie Redmayne: He won for playing Stephen Hawking in The Theory of Everything, after studying Hawking's movements and speech closely for the role.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Tom Hanks (first win): His win for Philadelphia was followed by another for Forrest Gump, making him the first back-to-back Best Actor winner since Spencer Tracy.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Leonardo DiCaprio: After several nominations, he finally won for The Revenant, a film shot in freezing conditions with natural light.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Frances McDormand (Nomadland): Her Nomadland win was her third acting Oscar, after Fargo and Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri; she also produced the film.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Henry Fonda: He won for On Golden Pond, his final film and only competitive acting Oscar; he was too ill to attend, so his daughter Jane accepted.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Jessica Tandy: She won for Driving Miss Daisy, becoming the oldest acting winner at the time, and the film also took Best Picture.
Age when they won the Best Actor/Actress.Anthony Hopkins (The Father): His win made him the oldest Best Actor winner ever; he also won for The Silence of the Lambs, with only about 16 minutes on screen.

Quentin Tarantino films by release.Reservoir Dogs: The jewel heist at the center of the film is never shown, and the criminals are known by color code names such as Mr. Pink.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Pulp Fiction: It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes, and revived John Travolta's career.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Jackie Brown: Adapted from Elmore Leonard's novel Rum Punch, it starred blaxploitation icon Pam Grier in the title role.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Kill Bill: Vol. 1: Tarantino originally made it as one film, but it was split into two, and its animated flashback was created by the Japanese studio Production I.G.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Kill Bill: Vol. 2: The sequel brings back the Bride's revenge in a slower, talkier film, including a scene where she is buried alive.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Death Proof: It was half of the Grindhouse double feature with Robert Rodriguez's Planet Terror, and stuntwoman Zoë Bell played herself.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Inglourious Basterds: Christoph Waltz won an Oscar as the menacing Nazi officer Hans Landa, and the film opens with a chilling farmhouse scene.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Django Unchained: It earned Tarantino an Oscar for original screenplay, and Waltz again won Best Supporting Actor.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.The Hateful Eight: It was shot in rare 70 mm film, and Ennio Morricone won his first competitive Oscar for its score.
Quentin Tarantino films by release.Once Upon a Time in Hollywood: Set in Los Angeles in 1969, it won Brad Pitt his first acting Oscar, and features a fictionalized Sharon Tate.

Waterbirds on the scale.Least sandpiper: The smallest of all shorebirds, it breeds on northern bogs and flies thousands of kilometres to winter in South America.
Waterbirds on the scale.Common kingfisher: Its beak shape inspired the nose of Japan's Shinkansen 500 series, designed to cut the thunderous boom in tunnels.
Waterbirds on the scale.Common tern: Terns are nicknamed sea swallows for their forked tails and graceful flight, and they plunge into the water to catch fish.
Waterbirds on the scale.Black-headed gull: Its head is actually chocolate-brown, and only in the breeding season; in winter the 'black' head is mostly white.
Waterbirds on the scale.Atlantic puffin: This stout seabird beats its wings up to around 400 times a minute and can carry many fish at once thanks to a spiny tongue.
Waterbirds on the scale.Mallard: This is the ancestor of nearly all domestic ducks, and the male's green head is structural colour, not pigment.
Waterbirds on the scale.Great blue heron: Hollow bones keep this bird light, so it spans nearly two metres of wing while weighing about as much as a bag of sugar.
Waterbirds on the scale.Canada goose: Flocks fly in a V because trailing birds ride the upwash from the bird ahead, which saves energy on long flights.
Waterbirds on the scale.Trumpeter swan: The largest native flying bird in North America was hunted nearly to extinction for its feathers and quills before recovering.
Waterbirds on the scale.Emperor penguin: Males balance a single egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter, fasting for about two months while they keep it warm.

When these went viral.Dancing Baby: A 3D-rendered cha-cha-dancing infant, it spread by email and then appeared on the TV show Ally McBeal.
When these went viral.Hampster Dance: Deidre LaCarte, a Canadian art student, made the page of dancing hamsters for a GeoCities contest with her sister.
When these went viral.Numa Numa: Gary Brolsma lip-synced to a Romanian pop hit, 'Dragostea din tei' by O-Zone, from his webcam.
When these went viral.Charlie Bit My Finger: The family took the video of two brothers down in 2021 after selling it as an NFT for about $760,000.
When these went viral.Double Rainbow: Paul Vasquez filmed a rainbow over Yosemite and, overcome, kept asking, 'What does it mean?'
When these went viral.Nyan Cat: A pixel cat with a Pop-Tart body trailing a rainbow, set to a looping Japanese song.
When these went viral.Gangnam Style: Psy's video was the first on YouTube to reach one billion views, and it overflowed YouTube's view counter.
When these went viral.Harlem Shake: Short 30-second videos began with someone dancing alone to Baauer's track, until the whole group erupted.
When these went viral.Ice Bucket Challenge: It raised over $100 million for ALS research in a single summer.
When these went viral.The Dress: Caitlin McNeill's photo split the internet over blue and black or white and gold; the actual dress was blue and black.

First time hosting the Oscars.Bob Hope: He hosted 19 times, a record, and was also known for entertaining troops overseas.
First time hosting the Oscars.Johnny Carson: He hosted five times from 1979 to 1984, and was famed as the host of The Tonight Show.
First time hosting the Oscars.Billy Crystal: He often opened with a film montage that inserted him into the year's Best Picture nominees.
First time hosting the Oscars.Whoopi Goldberg: She was the first woman to host the Oscars solo, and had won her own Oscar for Ghost in 1991.
First time hosting the Oscars.Steve Martin: Steve Martin's first hosting job came in 2001, and he later co-hosted with Alec Baldwin in 2010.
First time hosting the Oscars.Chris Rock: He returned to host again in 2016, a ceremony that came amid the #OscarsSoWhite controversy.
First time hosting the Oscars.Jon Stewart: He had been host of The Daily Show when he took the Oscar stage in 2006.
First time hosting the Oscars.Ellen DeGeneres: Her star-studded 2014 selfie became the most retweeted post at the time.
First time hosting the Oscars.Hugh Jackman: The Australian actor, a Tony winner, opened the 2009 show with a song-and-dance number.
First time hosting the Oscars.Jimmy Kimmel: At his first ceremony, a mix-up led La La Land to be named Best Picture before the error was corrected for Moonlight.

The year each TV show's story begins.Downton Abbey: Opens with news of the Titanic sinking in April 1912, which wipes out the heir and sets the family's inheritance plot in motion.
The year each TV show's story begins.Peaky Blinders: Loosely inspired by a real Birmingham street gang of the late 1800s, with the story moved to post-World War I Small Heath.
The year each TV show's story begins.Boardwalk Empire: Begins as Prohibition starts in Atlantic City. Boss Nucky Thompson is based on the real Enoch 'Nucky' Johnson.
The year each TV show's story begins.Band of Brothers: Follows Easy Company of the 506th Parachute Infantry from training in 1942. It was based on historian Stephen Ambrose's book.
The year each TV show's story begins.M*A*S*H (TV): Set in the Korean War of 1950 to 1953, yet the series ran eleven seasons, several times longer than the war itself.
The year each TV show's story begins.Mad Men: Opens in 1960 at a Madison Avenue ad agency with the Kennedy-Nixon election looming. Creator Matthew Weiner wrote it before The Sopranos.
The year each TV show's story begins.The Wonder Years: Adult Kevin Arnold, voiced by Daniel Stern, narrates his childhood in 1968, a year of upheaval across America.
The year each TV show's story begins.That '70s Show: Set in Point Place, Wisconsin. The pilot starts in 1976 and the story runs until the last day of 1979.
The year each TV show's story begins.Freaks and Geeks: Cancelled after 18 episodes, yet it launched Seth Rogen, James Franco, Jason Segel and Linda Cardellini.
The year each TV show's story begins.Stranger Things: Starts in Hawkins, Indiana, in November 1983 with a boy's disappearance. The Duffer Brothers modelled it on 1980s Spielberg and Stephen King.

When these drink and food packages appea.Mason jar patent: John Landis Mason's screw-top jar made home canning easy. Today it doubles as a drinking glass in hipster cafes.
When these drink and food packages appea.Paper drinking straw patent: Marvin Stone rolled paper around a pencil and glued it, because rye-grass straws left grit in his drink.
When these drink and food packages appea.Crown bottle cap: William Painter's crown cork, with its crimped metal edge, still seals most beer and soda bottles.
When these drink and food packages appea.Canned beer: The Gottfried Krueger Brewing Company sold the first cans in 1935. They were steel, with cone tops that needed a 'church key'.
When these drink and food packages appea.Tetra Pak carton: Founded by Sweden's Ruben Rausing. The name comes from the first package's tetrahedron shape.
When these drink and food packages appea.All-aluminum can: Coors introduced seamless aluminium cans in 1959. Aluminium recycles endlessly, and a can can be back on shelves in about two months.
When these drink and food packages appea.Pull-tab can: Ermal Fraze invented it after forgetting a can opener at a picnic, and had to open a beer on a car bumper.
When these drink and food packages appea.Bag-in-box wine: Australian Thomas Angove patented a plastic bladder inside a cardboard box for wine in 1965.
When these drink and food packages appea.PET plastic bottle patent: DuPont engineer Nathaniel Wyeth, brother of painter Andrew Wyeth, patented the plastic bottle that holds most soda.
When these drink and food packages appea.Stay-on can tab: Daniel Cudzik's design kept the tab attached, ending the era of detachable pull rings littering beaches and cutting feet.

Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Poppy seed: At week four the embryo is about a millimetre long, a tiny disc of cells that is just beginning to form the neural tube.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Blueberry: By week seven the embryo is around a centimetre long, and the face, with tiny pits for eyes and nostrils, has started to take shape.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Raspberry: At week eight, tiny fingers and toes are forming, and the embryo is moving, though far too slightly for anyone to feel.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Lime: By week twelve the baby's reflexes have begun, and it can curl its fingers, open its mouth and even suck its thumb.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Lemon: Around week fourteen, the baby can squint, grimace and frown, and the neck has lengthened so the head sits more upright.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Avocado: Around week sixteen, the baby's ears are in place and it begins to pick up muffled sounds, such as the mother's heartbeat.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Banana: Week twenty is the halfway mark, and the usual time for the detailed anomaly scan, when the baby is about 25 cm long.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Eggplant: At week 28 the third trimester begins, and the eyes can open and respond to light shining through the mother's abdomen.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Honeydew melon: By week 36 the lungs are nearly mature and the baby has put on plenty of fat; most settle head-down in the pelvis.
Baby's size during pregnancy, as fruit.Watermelon: At full term babies average about 3.4 kg and 50 cm, though a healthy newborn can be well above or below that average.

Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Sirius: The brightest star in the night sky; the name means 'scorching' in Greek, and it is the Dog Star.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Canopus: The second-brightest star, used by spacecraft as a navigation reference.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Alpha Centauri: It is the nearest star system, and Proxima Centauri orbits it.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Arcturus: A red giant about 37 light-years away, whose light was used to open the 1933 Chicago World's Fair.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Procyon: The 'Little Dog Star' has a faint white dwarf companion.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Altair: It spins so fast, completing a rotation in under ten hours, that it is visibly flattened.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Spica: Hipparchus used Spica's position to discover the precession of the equinoxes.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Deneb: A luminous supergiant and one of the most distant stars visible to the naked eye, thousands of light-years away.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Castor: This is a system of six stars, not one, and it is part of the Gemini twins.
Night-sky stars by how bright they look.Polaris: The North Star is not very bright; it is a pulsating Cepheid variable near the celestial pole.

When these animals were named by science.Javan rhino: There are fewer than 100 left, in Java's Ujung Kulon park.
When these animals were named by science.Pygmy hippo: This West African forest dweller is a tiny cousin of the common hippo.
When these animals were named by science.Przewalski's horse: It is named for a Russian explorer, and was reintroduced to Mongolia after nearly dying out.
When these animals were named by science.Mountain gorilla: Captain Robert von Beringe shot two in 1902, hence its Latin name Gorilla beringei.
When these animals were named by science.Mekong giant catfish: Some exceed 300 kg, and a 293 kg one caught in Thailand in 2005 is the heaviest on record.
When these animals were named by science.Kouprey: This wild ox of Cambodia has not been confirmed in the wild for decades, and may be extinct.
When these animals were named by science.Giant muntjac: Also called the large-antlered muntjac, it was found in Vietnam's Vu Quang forest.
When these animals were named by science.Kipunji: It formed a new genus of monkey, the first new African primate genus since 1923.
When these animals were named by science.Myanmar snub-nosed monkey: Its upturned nose is said to make it sneeze when rain falls.
When these animals were named by science.Tapanuli orangutan: Fewer than 800 survive in Sumatra, making it the most endangered great ape.

Night creatures by weight.Pipistrelle bat: One of the smallest bats in Europe, it can eat roughly 3,000 tiny insects in a single night, finding them by echolocation.
Night creatures by weight.Tarsier: Each of its eyes is about as large as its brain, which helps it hunt in the dark. It can swivel its head almost all the way around.
Night creatures by weight.Barn owl: Its heart-shaped face funnels sound to ears set at slightly different heights, so it can find prey in total darkness, and its flight is almost silent.
Night creatures by weight.Hedgehog: It has thousands of spines and rolls up for defence. It can also be a loud snuffler, and it hibernates through winter in Britain.
Night creatures by weight.Kiwi: The flightless bird has nostrils at the tip of its long beak to sniff out worms, and lays an egg that is huge compared to its body.
Night creatures by weight.Red fox: Foxes may use Earth's magnetic field to aim their pounce on prey hidden in grass. They are found across much of the northern hemisphere.
Night creatures by weight.Badger: Badgers live in underground setts that can be centuries old and have many rooms, passages and entrances. They are strongly social animals.
Night creatures by weight.Spotted hyena: Despite the myth that hyenas only scavenge, they hunt most of their own food. Females are larger and lead the clan, and the laugh-like call signals excitement.
Night creatures by weight.Lion: Lions are the only truly social big cats, and the females do most of the hunting. A male's roar can be heard from about eight kilometres away.
Night creatures by weight.Malayan tapir: Its black-and-white coat acts as camouflage in moonlight, breaking up its outline. Tapirs are related to horses and rhinos, and use their short trunk like a snorkel.

Where the new year arrives first.Kiritimati: Also called Christmas Island, this Kiribati atoll is among the first places to reach the new year and is the largest coral atoll by land area.
Where the new year arrives first.Auckland: Fireworks from the Sky Tower welcome the new year in New Zealand's biggest city, long before most of the world.
Where the new year arrives first.Sydney: Fireworks over the Sydney Harbour Bridge are a world-famous midnight show, broadcast around the globe.
Where the new year arrives first.Tokyo: Buddhist temples ring their bells 108 times, standing for human desires, in a ritual called Joya no Kane.
Where the new year arrives first.Delhi: India uses one time zone offset by half an hour, even though the country is wide enough to span two.
Where the new year arrives first.Dubai: The Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, hosts a vast light and fireworks show each New Year's Eve.
Where the new year arrives first.Paris: Crowds gather on the Champs-Elysees for the countdown, and the Arc de Triomphe is lit up for the occasion.
Where the new year arrives first.London: The Greenwich district of London defines the prime meridian, the zero line from which time zones are measured.
Where the new year arrives first.New York: A crystal ball has dropped over Times Square since 1907, watched by about a million people in the streets.
Where the new year arrives first.Honolulu: Hawaii is among the last to ring in the new year, by which time most of the world has already celebrated.
